messages:
Anna (SRE): ran a bunch of internal load tests this morning against the hosted API, trying to pick sane defaults for RPM/TPM and burst windows. posting raw numbers and a q for y'all :point_down:
Mike (Support): awesome, thanks. are these tests simulating real client behavior (bursty vs steady)?
Anna (SRE): yeah we did both. steady at 200 rps for 10m, and burst windows: 1k reqs in <2s, 10k over 1m, and some random spiky poisson profiles.
Julia (Platform): nice, curious what client patterns you used for auth token refreshes / retry logic — that changes observed error rates a lot.
Anna (SRE): used bearer tokens that don't expire during run. retried idempotent calls up to 2x with exponential backoff, 100ms -> 400ms. no client-side batching.
Kai (Perf): can you drop the key metrics? p99 latency, 5xx counts, 429s, CPU/GPU util, and queue/backlog numbers?
Anna (SRE): sure, pasted summary from ops-bot below.
ops-bot: loadtest-summary attached:
```
TEST: burst-1k-2s
DURATION: 120s
REQUESTS: 1,024
429s: 182 (17.8%)
5xx: 3
p50: 45ms p95: 120ms p99: 420ms
ingress qdepth peaks: 320
server cpu: 78% mem: 64%
```
ops-bot: and steady run:
```
TEST: steady-200rps-10m
REQUESTS: 120,000
429s: 0
5xx: 1
p50: 38ms p95: 110ms p99: 300ms
ingress qdepth avg: 28
server cpu: 62% mem: 59%
```
Mike (Support): that 17% 429 on the burst is the type of pattern customers keep opening tickets about. They see big upfront bursts during onboarding or scheduled sends.
Julia (Platform): what rate-limiter implementation was used? token-bucket? sliding window? per-key or global?
Anna (SRE): token-bucket on api-gw edge, per-api-key with global fallback. config for the run:
```yaml
edge_rate_limiter:
  policy: token_bucket
  rate_per_minute: 6000   # 100 rpm default in this test
  burst_tokens: 200       # allows some immediate short bursts
  window_seconds: 60
  enforcement: per_key
```
Kai (Perf): two quick notes: 1) burst_tokens=200 + client burst of 1k in 2s will hit token depletion instantly -> 429 avalanche. 2) the ingress qdepth 320 suggests we queue a lot in front of the runtime; that increases tail latency.
Mike (Support): so what should our default be to avoid 'surprising' 429s for onboarding spikes? Customers expect a short burst tolerance.
Julia (Platform): I'd propose: default rate_per_minute based on plan tier, but burst_tokens should be configurable with a short burst window separate from steady-state. e.g. burst_window_seconds=10 and allow burst_tokens = min(5% of monthly RPM, 2000).
Anna (SRE): idea: have two layers: edge token-bucket per_key with conservative steady rate, and a short-lived burst allowance from a shared reservoir per-customer that drains fast. fallback logic: accept burst up to shared reservoir then degrade to queued requests with low-priority.
Kai (Perf): +1. Also we should adjust request queuing: instead of piling to runtime when token-bucket denies, return a 429 with Retry-After and link to best-practices doc. queuing creates head-of-line problems.
Mike (Support): can we make Retry-After human-friendly? e.g. give both seconds and advice: "retry after 5s, or reduce concurrency to X". That cuts noise for support.
Anna (SRE): agreed. For load test recommendations to set SA: here's what I think we should standardize after these runs:
- default RPM per key (free tier): 100 RPM (1.6 RPS)
- default burst tokens: 300 with burst_window_seconds: 15
- aggressive tiers: 1000 RPM with burst_tokens: 2000
- shared short reservoir per-account: 5k tokens refilled at 1k/s for 30s after idle
- return 429 + Retry-After header + body with suggested concurrency and doc link
Julia (Platform): those numbers look reasonable but we need telemetry to validate. run instrumented load tests across 3 zones and with 100 synthetic keys that mimic customer onboarding: sudden 5k reqs over 20s across 50 keys.
Kai (Perf): I'll run a matrix overnight: parameters = [100,300,600,1000] RPM x [200,500,2000] burst x burst_window [5,15,60] and log p99/p95/429s and backlog. I'll also add client retry patterns (no retry, naive retry, jittered backoff).
ops-bot: scheduled perf-matrix job: run-id=pm-20260315-01 owner=Kai (Perf) ETA 8h :white_check_mark:
Mike (Support): once we have the matrix, can we produce a one-page support-friendly guidance (blurb + recommended plan defaults + troubleshooting steps)? I'll draft.
Anna (SRE): good. Also capture reproducible commands for the perf team. Example k6 snippet I used to reproduce the 1k/2s spike:
```bash
k6 run --vus 1000 --duration 10s spike_test.js
# spike_test.js: send single-shot bursts, no retry, oauth header
```
Julia (Platform): one more operational item: add an event in the console when a key hits >50% of its shared reservoir within 60s so customers can proactively throttle or upgrade. saves support tickets.
Kai (Perf): noted. I'll upload the raw matrix CSV + summary at the end of the run and mark the parameter set that hits <1% 429 while keeping p99 < 500ms as candidate defaults.
Anna (SRE): sweet. next steps: Kai runs matrix; Julia adds console signal + config knobs; Mike drafts support guidance; I'll update rate-limiter code PR with dual-reservoir prototype.
Mike (Support): thanks team. cc @product for visibility - this will help reduce onboarding tickets massively. :tada:
Anna (SRE): filing follow-ups: link to PR and artifacts will be posted here when ready. closing loop later today. :eyes:
